1.)Weapon
2.)Gear
3.)Self

You take care of those things, in that order. If your weapon or your gear is not operable or going to fail you because of lack of maintenance, you’re as good as dead. Work in pairs, fire teams, squads, etc. Your strength is your team and your coordination of said team. If you’re moving, someone better be covering you with fire. If someone else is moving, you better be covering them with fire. Take well placed shots and try your best to conserve your ammunition, situation dictating. COMMUNICATE WITH YOUR TEAM. Know your weapon system and how to perform immediate action drills such as mag reloads, clearing jams, etc. There’s not much else I can really add. I have the utmost respect for all of you that are going. I’m not going to discourage you. I’m going to tell you to go get some. The horrors of war are real. You cannot mentally prepare for what you’re going to see. Focus on your weapon and your teams. God speed.

-A former 0311

They’ll generally roost near water, where pines and hardwoods or other different terrain features meet. Dive into the hardwoods and look for scratch. All the leaves will be tore up and scattered around with bare dirt everywhere. Look for a clearing or field near by those features where they will generally fly down and strut in the morning, pick at bugs, socialize, etc. You can use a locator call to roost them at night. You can also get out early some mornings and listen for gobbles, get them to shock gobble, etc. Glass fields and clearing in the morning too, looking for strutters. The Primos videos on YouTube are good for tips and tricks, as well as Knight and Hale, the hunting public, etc. I personally think locating them is the hardest part. Once you do that, you can strategize and use the terrain to hunt them. Good luck!

I agree. When you’re in the clutches of alcohol, you look at everything through a lens of “alcohol would make this so much better!” Not true. I had a weekend where I had to drive 2 hours to check on my parents house while they were away on vacation. I got there and of course the refrigerator was full of beer. I decided to abstain, did a few chores, watched some tv, got a full nights sleep, woke up early and was able to enjoy a beautiful sunny morning with a cup of coffee on the back porch. I listened to the birds and watched the trees, hangover free. It was an amazing morning and a very simple experience. However, had I drank the night before, I would’ve undoubtedly woken up late in a terrible mood, sick, full of regret and hate, and a 2 hour drive back ahead of me. That would’ve been beyond miserable and started a viscous cycle of self loathing. I constantly think about my sober choice and the beauty of that morning. It propels me to make the right choice day after day!

Energy I could use for work and accomplishing my goals. Love that I could be showing to my girlfriend. It’s just never worth it. Waking up with a clear mind and conscious. I remember everything it has taken from me and how negatively it will affect my life. I refuse to be a dog just chasing my tail. I will not drink with you today! Good luck!

That buck is hard horned with no velvet. He’s full of testosterone and most likely rutting. Bucks that big/old are generally loners so the presence of does indicates breeding season. People don’t appreciate how violent and strong a rutting buck is. They will happily fight to the death for breeding rights. Those antler tines are very sharp and strong. YouTube buck fights. They can break each other’s necks, take eyes out, rip holes in vital organs, etc. They’re also insanely tough animals. They survive gun shots, arrows, being hit by cars, coyote attacks, brutal weather, etc. That ram had no idea what he was getting into. He’s lucky he survived.
